idiom_name: Slick filter(id, version).update(...) returning affectedRowsCount (Doobie or JDBC the same) + AtomicLong on the JVM
implementation_notes: Slick has no optimistic-locking feature, but its update action already supplies the missing half: build the query with the version predicate - books.filter(b => b.id === id && b.version === expected).map(b => (b.title, b.version)).update((title, expected + 1)) - and treat the Int returned by db.run as the affected-rows count, where 0 is the conflict; the same shape is expressed in Doobie or plain JDBC with the predicate in the WHERE clause. For in-memory state on the JVM the token is an AtomicLong (or an STM ref with a single writer) and compareAndSet is the test. Akka/Pekko persistence offers a related but different token - the event sequence number a command expects - which is the same idea pushed into the aggregate rather than the row.
pitfalls: Slick updates may only touch raw columns of a single table; anything involving joins or computed values must be hand-written SQL with the predicate restated.
The version comparison is lifted (===), not Scala ==, and mixing the two either fails to compile or compares the wrong thing.
Running the read and the conditional write as independent Futures lets them land on different transactions; keep them in one DBIO action or one transaction.
